notes: Read SKILL.md and references/details.md in full. The skill summarizes PCI DSS (the 12 requirement headings, merchant levels, SAQ types) and gives Python samples for data minimization and log masking, processor tokenization, a Fernet token vault, AES-GCM encryption at rest, secure cookies/HTTPS, role-gated access, audit logging, Luhn validation and a compliance checklist.
No commands, installs, credentials, or network access; samples are application code with placeholder Stripe keys (pk_..., sk_...).

The 12-requirement list (SKILL.md:20-50) is a set of one-line headings in PCI DSS v3.2.1 wording, not reproduced standard text; v4.0 renamed several requirements, so verify against the current standard. The tokenization sample uses Stripe's legacy Tokens/Charges APIs; `sanitize_input` is an empty stub; the AES-GCM usage generates a throwaway key (SKILL.md:251), so real deployments need managed keys. This is guidance, not a compliance attestation.
